correctness.rationale: A complete elementary proof gives each section as a cube–simplex Minkowski sum and constructs its subset-inequality converse, then proves every inequality is a full facet. The inball upper bound uses lower-coordinate facets and the two opposite full-set inequalities; attaining the bound forces t=1/2 and every other coordinate equal to the radius. The strict monotonicity of the normalized subset barriers proves feasibility and exact tangencies. Complementary Boolean vertex pairs force exact diameter and circumball. Slice decomposition proves the volume integral, with a nondegenerate Laplace maximum for k=2. A standalone checker independently ran 103232 finite assertions, facet rank and LP tests on five parameter cases; finite checks are not substituted for the proof.

value.rationale: Yang’s Boolean 0/1-polytopes disprove universal graph edge expansion; whether those counterexamples are geometrically thin or have overly intricate facet boundaries is a natural structural question. The complete irredundant facet count shows the original poor-expansion examples have just 10n+2 facets in dimension 4n+1 (about 2.5 facets per dimension); the exact unique inball retains over 80% of the ambient cube inradius, while maximal diameter and exponentially small ambient volume coexist. The wider block-dimension formula explains the precise retention curve, down to a quarter-unit radius. These constitute nontrivial all-dimensional metric and facet classifications with a clear use in understanding the counterexample family, not merely a code or normalization check.
